item.title: NBA legend Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu mansion listed for $48 million after massive makeover
item.description: NBA legend Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu mansion is now listed for $48 million after a major transformation. Garnett purchased the Pacific Coast Highway property for $6.4 million in 2003 and began building a custom home that remained unfinished. Following a failed $16 million sale and legal disputes, the estate was completed and transformed into a luxury residence.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: A dying mother’s wish protects 2,506 acres ranch
item.description: David Ellsbury honored his late mother's wish by safeguarding the family's cherished Diamond E Ranch from development. Spanning 2,506 acres, this land is now forever shielded by a land trust, ensuring that future generations can enjoy its unspoiled beauty. The ranching traditions of the family will thrive on this preserved estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 5 migrants dead after boat carrying over 100 people drifts for weeks in Atlantic
item.description: At least five African migrants died after their boat encountered trouble at sea. Forty-four survivors were rescued and brought to safety near Gran Canaria. Survivors reported being adrift for nearly a month without provisions. Many migrants suffered dehydration and illness after drinking seawater. The Atlantic route to the Canary Islands remains a dangerous journey.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Kodak retiree finds new animal in moss from New York log; scientists confirm it as a new tardigrade
item.description: A retired Kodak finance worker and longtime volunteer, Judy Dobles, discovered a previously unknown tardigrade species after collecting moss from a log at New York’s Cumming Nature Center and examining it under a microscope. The species was formally recognised about a year later. Named Mesocrista ojagwaji, it adds to the growing list of tardigrades identified in New York and highlights how much microscopic life remains to be studied.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Warming peatlands can turn them from carbon sinks to leaks
item.description: Peatlands, which store significant global soil carbon, are now releasing it. Warming temperatures cause these ecosystems to shift from carbon accumulators to emitters. This transition occurs rapidly, even with modest warming of four degrees Fahrenheit. Researchers observed carbon loss rates significantly faster than historical accumulation rates. These findings impact global climate forecasting models and future predictions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: An elderly San Francisco woman mailed checks to pay her bills; thieves took $14,000 from her
item.description: A woman lost fourteen thousand dollars when thieves intercepted her mailed cheques, tampered with the information, and cashed them. This incident sheds light on the escalating issue of mail theft and cheque washing in the Bay Area. Authorities note a concerning rise in mail theft incidents from both postal collection and home mailboxes. For seniors relying on cheques, retrieving lost funds can be particularly challenging.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2005, Virginia bought 431 waterfront acres for a future state park; 21 years later...
item.description: A 431-acre waterfront parcel in Gloucester County has been officially added to Machicomoco State Park. This undeveloped land, purchased over two decades ago, will now serve as Machicomoco's Western Unit. A newly approved 30-year master plan outlines development phases for both park sections. However, no state funding has been allocated for any of the proposed improvements. Public access to the Western Unit remains restricted, awaiting future financial commitments.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1999, scientists dropped 45 tons of wollastonite over a 29-acre New Hampshire watershed
item.description: In an ambitious forest restoration initiative in New Hampshire, researchers sought to mitigate the effects of acid rain. They introduced calcium-rich minerals, leading to an initial boost in tree vitality and growth. However, this solution inadvertently resulted in a staggering increase in nitrogen levels in nearby streams, releasing thirty times more inorganic nitrogen compared to untreated regions. This outcome underscores the intricate dynamics of ecosystems in response to human intervention.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Off-grid Az ranch for sale: 'It's ready for zombie apocalypse'
item.description: Bob Worsley, the visionary behind SkyMall, is parting ways with his picturesque family ranch in Heber, Arizona. Spanning 35 acres, this stunning off-grid estate features a spacious lodge, several cabins, and boasts complete self-sufficiency with solar energy and its own well. The property offers a refreshing retreat from the desert's swelter and includes a natural gathering lake. It's currently on the market for $9.475 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: ‘Diversity is true beauty of society’: B'desh PM extends Janmashtami greetings
item.description: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman extended Janmashtami greetings to the Hindu community. He stated that the country belongs to all citizens, who enjoy equal rights. Rahman urged strengthening religious harmony, tolerance, and mutual respect among people. He warned against forces attempting to create divisions and communal tensions. The Prime Minister distributed honorariums to priests and sebaits.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: American Ex Navy man finds his Japanese first love after 70 years
item.description: After a heart-wrenching separation of nearly seventy years, Duane Mann and Peggy Yamaguchi finally found each other again. Believing his savings vanished and letters silenced, Mann discovered his mother had hidden their correspondence by burning Peggy's letters. Tragically, Peggy had endured the loss of their child and moved on with another. Their reunion brought long-awaited closure, reaffirming the deep bond and affection that still lingered between them.

item.title: Woman's family joked about her looking 'nothing' like her siblings, then a DNA test revealed something even more shocking
item.description: A family joke about adoption unexpectedly became reality for Payton Lee after a DNA test. The test revealed she shared a different father than her four younger siblings. This discovery meant the man she knew as Dad for twenty-nine years was not her biological father. Her father reacted with understanding, stating their relationship remained unchanged. Payton now advises caution when taking home DNA tests for casual fun.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet 16-year-old Pennsylvania student who opened his second restaurant while still in high school
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Gage Klein is already running his second restaurant in Pennsylvania while continuing high school. He recently opened Driftwood at the Fairgrounds in West York, after launching his first restaurant, Driftwood at the Lake, more than a year ago. With his father Kris helping with the business, Klein plans to attend culinary school after graduation and hopes to open more restaurants in the future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
